claims.text: The as-deposited material is a non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy-alloy thin film.
The as-deposited film has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited film contains local chemical disorder at grain boundaries.
Rapid thermal annealing near 500°C changes the degree of nanoscale chemical ordering in the film.
An intermediate annealing duration produces an optimal degree of nanoscale chemical ordering.
The relevant structural mediator is short-range chemical ordering at grain boundaries.
Changes in local chemical order adjust magnetoelastic coupling.
Optimal nanoscale chemical ordering lowers the nucleation barrier for the magnetostructural transformation.
An intermediate degree of ordering distributes the phase transformation over a wider temperature range.
Distributing the transformation over a wider temperature range reduces the sharpness and hysteresis of the entropy-change response.
A film annealed near 500°C for approximately 5 minutes will have a broader magnetostructural transition than the as-deposited film.
A film annealed near 500°C for approximately 5 minutes will have lower transition hysteresis than the as-deposited film.
Moderate annealing will cause a modest reduction in the maximum magnetic entropy change.
Too-short or too-long annealing will produce a sharper transition and larger hysteretic losses than moderate annealing.
Excessive grain growth may exacerbate transition sharpness or hysteretic losses.
As-deposited films display a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition with a significant but abrupt entropy change.
The as-deposited thin films have limited heat-exchange efficiency because of a low surface-to-volume ratio.
The predictions apply to annealing durations of 1–10 minutes near 500°C when grain size is held constant or its changes are monitored.
If magnetocaloric variations correlate only with grain size and not with chemical ordering, chemical ordering is not the governing variable proposed by the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline attributes limited heat exchange and a low surface-to-volume ratio to thin films. This is internally implausible for the proposed thin-film geometry and appears to transfer a limitation stated for bulk ingots or ribbons to the film baseline without justification.
